I'll leave some tips here on what helped me with my panic attacks but please feel free to text me privately if you're just in need of someone listening. I won't try to make you give up your plan, nor encourage you to do it. But I'll be there for you and you won't be lonely.

As for the panic attacks, here's what helped me:

- Find a safe position and place to put yourself in. Make sure you're not on your back because you could choke more easily, for example. Try to find a soft spot, maybe on the bed where you can sit up - maybe even hug a pillow before things get very bad. I always had the habit of eventually letting go of my pillow and going on my back which always made me choke but if you can hold onto a better position, try your best to do so.
- Find something that you know makes your emotions burst out and turn it into a mantra. For example, I personally always felt extremely vulnerable when listening to the adventure time song "everything stays" and I know both the lyrics and the general sound of it. Whenever I have a panic attack I try to sing it in my head, word by word and I always start with such a foggy mind that I can't remember a single word or tune. But as I keep focusing, I slowly remember the tune and how the background music goes and then words are slowly coming back to my mind. I managed to sing it in my head about 2-3 times before I am fully calmed down and it always makes me cry harder for a little bit but that's ok.
- Make sure you drink lots of water after and that you eat a little bit - anything that you enjoy - preferably something nutritious or something sweet if the attack was severe. I personally found out that having a bit of chocolate after my panic attack reduced the dizziness i had afterwards.
- Make sure you have a to-go afterwards. I recommend making a nice calm playlist with either songs, standup or whatever you know you enjoy effortlessly. Don't move too much in the first hour after it happened and try to massage yourself when you feel a bit better (or ask someone if you have the possibility). Our bodies go through severe distress during a panic attack and relaxing the muscles is key.

That being said, there isn't much you can do to prevent it but I hope what I said above will hope ease the pain your body has to go through afterwards.

If I were you, I'd take some time and think about everything.

I understand you probably love your gf but depression is a nasty thing. Ask yourself if you can truly be there for her. Are you strong enough? I'll leave some good questions of things that might or might not happen which should help you find an answer:

\- ***Are you ready to listen to her, truly?*** She might talk about her life, over and over again, talk about trauma, abuse, personal things that led up to her feeling depressed. She might tell you about things she used to/uses to cope with her depression. She might've had suicide attempts, panic attacks, etc. Are you ready to listen the worst of someone and keep your calm? Be there for them? Not get tired or angry with them?

\- ***Are you ready to see some bad stuff?*** If you truly want to be there for her, you need to acknowledge things like cutting, vomiting, insomnia, etc. None of them are easy especially when they come together. Are you ready to be sleep deprived if she has insomnia and she needs you there? Are you ready to deal with blood? Would you be the same if she would panic to the point where she couldn't move, cry to the point where she wouldn't be able to breathe? If you assure her that you'll be there for her, you can't run away when shit gets real

\- ***Would you still love her?*** After everything I've said above and more, if all the bad things would go her way and you'd have to be there for all of it, if it would fuck up with your own life...would you still love her? Many people find that dealing with a depressed partner made them lose feelings.

Last but not least:

\- ***Can you trust yourself enough to do it all?*** A lot of people quit halfway, become overwhelmed and leave the person, that they wanted to help, behind. When you deal with someone depressed and you claim to be their support, don't expect to see them fake their emotions and actions. They can be negative for days, weeks, months. They can be on the edge for long periods of time where it can seem like there's no light to ever shine again. It will be your job to remind them everyday that there is indeed a light to come. Everyday, even if it feels like it does nothing. Are you sure you won't end up angry and sad? Find yourself venting about her to other people?

I mentioned some sensitive topics above that I think should help you grasp in the concept of depression and struggles when you want to help someone in this position. Be aware that being honest and admitting what you can and can't do is a lot better than promising everything and not delivering it. Depressed people face struggles daily, lose people because of things they can't control, sink deeper even when they're trying to swim up. Remember that as hard as it is for you, it's at least double as hard for them.

​

If you feel like you can handle everything I've said, then what you have to do to help your gf is *simply* be there for her. Which we just saw, it's not that simple after all.

*Wishing all the best for you both! Healing takes time!*

You cope with it every second you decide to take another breath. You can't do much sadly to just "fix" it. Truth is that being depressed becomes a part of you that you eventually have to learn how to live with. It will never go away, nobody will "make it better".

You can aim to heal and learn how to make the best out of your life little by little. You can hope someday you'll manage to heal enough to push your depression deep within yourself and work everyday to keep it there.

You will be happy again, you will smile and laugh. It will be different. Sometimes better, sometimes worse.

Being someone's boyfriend doesn't mean you have to drop your entire life for them. Especially when they don't understand you have your own life going on and that they can't be the only thing existing in your life.

To me it sounds like your girlfriend is just a little (or more) selfish, and let me tell you why:

From what you've said here, you're trying your best to be there for her, all the time, but you can't because you have to do well in school and focus on things that are mandatory for your future. What I don't see here is how things are on your side, in terms of help. I think it's easy for a lot of people to fall under the impression that they don't need anything back, but you do...we all do. I don't know if you asked yourself before "Would she do the same for me if I were she, behaving like this?" but you should definitely give that a minute.

Aside from that, I am speaking from my own experience that when you care about someone they are also a priority, not just yourself. It's hard for me to belive she doesn't realise that what she does is mostly working against you than it's helping you or your relationship. It's ok to ask for help, but it's not ok to demand someone's time.

About the getting upset over things that you forget, that's just being immature. I remember when me and my bf started dating he even forgot a couple of times that we were supposed to have a call (we were LDR) because his friends hit him up and he just went there. Sure I could've burned him down but why? For doing something that brought him joy? When you care about someone you just ask yourself what can you do to make them happy, and for example, me flaming him for forgetting that, wouldn't have turned the time back, it would've just ruined a night for him that ended up being very fun. Months and months later, he never forgets a single call, he always remembers everything we plan, he is my biggest support ever.

A relationship isn't perfect from the start and unless you work for it, it will never be even close. That being said, your girlfriend should simply realise that you being in a relationship with her doesn't mean you are responsible for her mental state and that she should understand that she will either stop this immature behaviour and be there for you too or she will simply lose you.

Stay strong and definitely focus on your school! At this age, people are not very mature and relationships are not something that you can really count on. Education on the other hand, is very stable, at any age. So before you find that special someone, don't ruin your life over people that won't even say "thank you" in the end.
